### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A25's outgoing transitions were spread almost evenly over A35, A36, A41, A42 and A43 (about 18–23% each, out of roughly 200 observed outgoing transitions); in the later window, about 96% of A25's outgoing transitions go to A27. [DIR001]
- A26 shows the mirror image: earlier, about 98% of its outgoing transitions went to A30; in the later window, they are spread over the same five activities (about 16–22% each). [DIR002]
- All five block activities changed their exit: earlier, each sent about 16–21% of its outgoing transitions to A27; in the later window, A27 is no longer observed as their successor and A30 appears at about 18–22%, while their transitions among themselves stay broadly similar. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- The order between the block and A26/A27 flipped almost completely: earlier, each block activity ran before A26 in about 97–99% of the 200 traces and before A27 in about 97–99%; in the later window, A26 and A27 each run before the block activities in about 96–98%. The five activities still co-occur with A26 in 100% of traces in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- Mean relative position moved accordingly: A26 from about 0.65 to 0.52 of the trace, A27 from about 0.52 to 0.39, and each block activity from about 0.44 to about 0.60; all six activities occur in essentially every trace in both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- Adjacencies changed to match: in the later window, A27 immediately follows A25 (distance 1 in about 97% of 199 traces), A26 is followed within five steps by each block activity (about 194–196 traces each) and each block activity is followed by A30 (about 195–197 traces each) — pairs seen in only 1–2 traces earlier. The earlier adjacencies, A25 followed by each block activity and each block activity followed by A27 (about 193–197 traces each), are nearly gone in the later window (1–2 traces each). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG016, LAG017, LAG018, LAG019]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the five-activity block A35, A36, A41, A42 and A43 changed its placement in the flow. In the earlier window the fragment ran from A25 into the block and from the block into A27, with A26 leading almost always directly to A30; in the later window, A25 leads directly to A27, A26 leads into the block, and the block leads into A30 — the block now sits after A26 (and, by mean positions, after A27 and A26, which kept their mutual order) instead of between A25 and A27. That this ensemble is not what a stable process produces is supported by the screening result: 43 control-flow items qualified where about 0.8 were expected without change among 160 tested units. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG016, LAG017, LAG018, LAG019]

The change is shown directly and consistently: the successor profiles of A25 and A26 exchanged shapes, all five block activities replaced A27 with A30 as an exit on about 200 outgoing transitions each, the order flips are near-complete while co-occurrence stays at 100% (so nothing became optional or rarely co-occurring), and the adjacency and position evidence agree with the rewiring. A27 and A30 both exist in both windows; what changed is their upstream connections, and the block's internal transition pattern is similar in both windows. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, LAG001, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG013, LAG015, LAG017, LAG019, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

Limitations: the evidence is aggregate and pairwise, so the full end-to-end arrangement is not directly observed — in particular, the relative order of A25, A27 and A26 in the later window rests on mean event positions — and the data cannot distinguish whether the block moved downstream or A25/A26 together with A27/A30 exchanged connection roles; both readings fit the same relations. LAG items backed by only 1–2 observations in a window were not relied upon. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG011, LAG012, LAG014, LAG016, LAG018]

Other differences: beyond the rewiring above, only rare transitions of about 1 in 200 outgoing transitions around A25 and A26 changed (for example, A25's infrequent edges to A49, A31, A08 and A13 earlier versus A19, A20, A26, A29, A39 and A47 later); they accompany the same change rather than forming a separate difference. [DIR001, DIR002]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

We have 200 traces before, 200 after. Screening: 160 units tested, 43 items qualified, 0.8 expected without change. That's a count many times larger than the expectation (43 vs 0.8), so the evidence as a whole cannot be explained by chance. So we're not in "insufficient evidence" territory by the screening comparison.

All evidence is control-flow family (DIR, POS, REL, LAG). No time items (TWAIT), no resource items (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources.

Let me understand the pattern.

DIR items (outgoing transition distributions of source activities):

- DIR001: source A25. Before: outgoing transitions spread across A41 (~0.23), A42 (~0.18), A35 (~0.18), A43 (~0.20), A36 (~0.19), plus tiny bits. After: A27 dominates at ~0.96, everything else tiny. So A25 now almost always leads to A27, whereas before it led to a spread of activities (A41, A42, A35, A43, A36 roughly equally). Support: 204 before, 203 after — substantial.

- DIR002: source A26. Before: A30 ~0.975 dominant. After: spread across A35 (~0.20), A42 (~0.22), A41 (~0.21), A43 (~0.16), A36 (~0.19), A30 tiny. So A26 used to go almost always to A30; now it goes to a spread of A35/A36/A41/A42/A43. Support 202/203.

- DIR003: source A35. Before: A43 ~0.23, A42 ~0.19, A27 ~0.16, A36 ~0.19, A41 ~0.19 spread. After: A42 ~0.22, A30 ~0.18, A41 ~0.19, A43 ~0.18, A36 ~0.18 spread; A27 gone (dropped to ~0.005), A30 appeared. So A27 as successor of A35 disappeared, A30 appeared.

- DIR004: source A36. Before: A27 ~0.21, A41 ~0.17, A35 ~0.15, A42 ~0.24, A43 ~0.19. After: A41 ~0.21, A35 ~0.20, A43 ~0.20, A42 ~0.19, A30 ~0.18; A27 gone, A30 appeared.

- DIR005: source A41. Before: A35 ~0.23, A43 ~0.23, A27 ~0.17, A42 ~0.17, A36 ~0.17. After: A43 ~0.18, A36 ~0.22, A42 ~0.17, A30 ~0.20, A35 ~0.21; A27 gone, A30 appeared.

- DIR006: source A42. Before: A36 ~0.21, A41 ~0.18, A35 ~0.25, A27 ~0.19, A43 ~0.13. After: A36 ~0.14, A43 ~0.25, A41 ~0.14, A35 ~0.20, A30 ~0.22; A27 gone, A30 appeared.

- DIR007: source A43. Before: A42 ~0.20, A36 ~0.20, A27 ~0.21, A41 ~0.19, A35 ~0.16. After: A30 ~0.20, A41 ~0.22, A35 ~0.16, A42 ~0.16, A36 ~0.24; A27 gone, A30 appeared.

So the pattern: before, A25 led to a spread {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} (each ~0.18–0.23), and each of A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 led (partly) to A27, and A26 led to A30. After, A25 leads almost always to A27 (~0.96), and A26 leads to the spread {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43}, and each of A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 now leads to A30 instead of A27.

Hmm, interesting. So it looks like A25 and A26 swapped roles? Before: A25 → {A35..A43} → A27; A26 → A30. After: A25 → A27; A26 → {A35..A43} → A30.

Wait, let me re-check. Before:
- A25 → spread over A41, A42, A35, A43, A36 (each ~0.18–0.23).
- A26 → A30 (~0.975).
- A35 → A43, A42, A27, A36, A41 (A27 ~0.16).
- A36 → A27 ~0.21, others.
- A41 → A27 ~0.17.
- A42 → A27 ~0.19.
- A43 → A27 ~0.21.

After:
- A25 → A27 (~0.96).
- A26 → spread over A35, A42, A41, A43, A36 (each ~0.16–0.22).
- A35 → A42, A30, A41, A43, A36 (A30 ~0.18, A27 ~0).
- A36 → A41, A35, A43, A42, A30 (A30 ~0.18, A27 ~0).
- A41 → A43, A36, A42, A30, A35 (A30 ~0.20, A27 ~0).
- A42 → A36, A43, A41, A35, A30 (A30 ~0.22, A27 ~0).
- A43 → A30, A41, A35, A42, A36 (A30 ~0.20, A27 ~0).

So indeed: the "spread" outgoing behaviour moved from A25 to A26, and the "single successor" behaviour moved from A26 to A25. And the successor A27 (of the middle group) was replaced by A30.

POS items:

- POS001: A26 mean position 0.649 → 0.520 (decreased ~0.13).
- POS002: A27 mean 0.516 → 0.388 (decreased ~0.13).
- POS003: A35 mean 0.442 → 0.597 (increased ~0.15).
- POS004: A36 mean 0.445 → 0.595 (increased ~0.15).
- POS005: A41 mean 0.442 → 0.595 (increased ~0.15).
- POS006: A42 mean 0.440 → 0.597 (increased ~0.16).
- POS007: A43 mean 0.439 → 0.599 (increased ~0.16).

So A26 and A27 moved earlier (position decreased), while A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 moved later (position increased by ~0.15). Support 200/200 for all — these activities occur in essentially all traces.

REL items (pairs with A26 or A27):

- REL001: A26 vs A35: before B_before_A = 0.985 (A35 before A26), after A_before_B = 0.98 (A26 before A35). Order flipped.
- REL002: A26 vs A36: before A36 before A26 (0.985), after A26 before A36 (0.96). Flipped.
- REL003: A26 vs A41: before A41 before A26 (0.97), after A26 before A41 (0.975). Flipped.
- REL004: A26 vs A42: before A42 before A26 (0.985), after A26 before A42 (0.975). Flipped.
- REL005: A26 vs A43: before A43 before A26 (0.98), after A26 before A43 (0.975). Flipped.
- REL006: A27 vs A35: before A35 before A27 (0.99), after A27 before A35 (0.98). Flipped.
- REL007: A27 vs A36: before A36 before A27 (0.99), after A27 before A36 (0.97). Flipped.
- REL008: A27 vs A41: before A41 before A27 (0.975), after A27 before A41 (0.98). Flipped.
- REL009: A27 vs A42: before A42 before A27 (0.99), after A27 before A42 (0.98). Flipped.
- REL010: A27 vs A43: before A43 before A27 (0.985), after A27 before A43 (0.98). Flipped.

So before: A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 all executed before A26 and before A27. After: A26 and A27 both executed before A35, A36, A41, A42, A43.

LAG items: these are about distances between ordered pairs within five steps. Many have very low support in one window (1 or 2 observations), so treat as weak. Let me look at the ones with substantial support:

- LAG001: A25→A27: before support 1 (only 1 observation), after support 199 with lag 1 in 97% of cases. So after, A27 immediately follows A25 (distance 1) in nearly all cases. Before, this pair within 5 steps was observed only once. Weak before, strong after.
- LAG007: A26→A35: before support 1 (lag 2), after support 195 spread across lags 1–5. So after, A35 follows A26 within 5 steps in nearly all traces, at varying distance. Before, observed once.
- LAG008: A26→A36: before support 2, after 194 spread.
- LAG009: A26→A42: before support 1 (lag 4), after 195 spread.
- LAG010: A26→A43: before support 1 (lag 3), after 196 spread.
- LAG013: A36→A30: before support 1 (lag 5), after 195 spread.
- LAG015: A41→A30: before support 2, after 197 spread.
- LAG017: A42→A30: before support 1 (lag 3), after 195 spread.
- LAG019: A43→A30: before support 1 (lag 4), after 197 spread.

The ones with high before support and low after support:
- LAG002: A25→A35: before 193 spread, after 1 (lag 3).
- LAG003: A25→A36: before 197 spread, after 2.
- LAG004: A25→A41: before 197, after 2.
- LAG005: A25→A42: before 197, after 1.
- LAG006: A25→A43: before 196, after 2.
- LAG011: A35→A27: before 196 spread, after 1 (lag 3).
- LAG012: A36→A27: before 195 spread, after 1 (lag 5).
- LAG014: A41→A27: before 193 spread, after 1 (lag 1).
- LAG016: A42→A27: before 197, after 1 (lag 2).
- LAG018: A43→A27: before 193, after 1 (lag 4).

So the LAG evidence confirms: before, A25 was followed (within 5 steps) by each of A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 in nearly all traces; after, that pattern disappeared (support 1–2). Conversely, after, A25 is followed immediately by A27 (LAG001, support 199, lag 1 in 97%), and A26 is followed by each of A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 (LAG007–LAG010, support ~194–196). Also after, each of A35, A36, A41, A42, A43 is followed by A30 (LAG013, LAG015, LAG017, LAG019, support ~195–197); before, those pairs were observed once or twice. Before, each of A35–A43 was followed by A27 (LAG011, LAG012, LAG014, LAG016, LAG018, support ~193–197); after, support 1.

So the overall picture is a consistent structural change: the roles of A25 and A26 swapped, and A27 was replaced by A30 as the activity following the middle group.

Let me reconstruct the process fragment:

Before:
- A25 branches to one of {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} (roughly equally, ~20% each).
- That chosen activity then leads to A27 (each with ~16–21% of their outgoing transitions going to A27; the rest going elsewhere — hmm, wait).

So A35 leads to A27 only 16% of the time; it also leads to A42, A43, A36, A41. Hmm, that suggests the middle group {A35, A36, A41, A42, A43} may be executed in some order/loop among themselves, and eventually A27.
